Renders the system Apple Pay button. Only available on iOS.

Prop Type Required Description buttonType ApplePayButtonType Yes Button label type. buttonStyle ApplePayButtonStyle Yes Visual style. onPress () => void, wrapped with callback() No Called when the user taps the button. Must be wrapped, see Nitro and onPress. style ViewStyle No Layout/style (e.g. width, height). ApplePayButtonType: 'buy' | 'setUp' | 'book' | 'donate' | 'continue' | 'reload' | 'addMoney' | 'topUp' | 'order' | 'rent' | 'support' | 'contribute' | 'tip' ApplePayButtonStyle: 'white' | 'whiteOutline' | 'black'

import { ApplePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' import { callback } from 'react-native-nitro-modules' const handlePayment = async () => { // Call startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout here } <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={callback(handlePayment)} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} />

ApplePayButton is a Nitro view, so onPress must be wrapped with callback() from react-native-nitro-modules. A bare function does not reach the native button, and tapping it does nothing. See Troubleshooting: Nitro callback for onPress.
Renders the Google Pay button. Only available on Android.

Prop Type Required Description buttonType GooglePayButtonType Yes Button label type. theme 'dark' | 'light' Yes Button theme. radius number No Corner radius in dp. supportedNetworks string[] No The card networks your payment accepts, as in PaymentRequest.supportedNetworks. Default: visa, mastercard, amex, discover. googlePayAllowedAuthMethods string[] No As in PaymentRequest.googlePayAllowedAuthMethods. Default: both. merchantCapabilities string[] No As in PaymentRequest.merchantCapabilities. 'Debit' without 'Credit' leaves credit cards out. Default: every card type. onPress () => void, wrapped with callback() No Called when the user taps the button. Must be wrapped, see Nitro and onPress. style ViewStyle No Layout/style (e.g. width, height). The button can show the payer's card, so give it the same supportedNetworks, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods and merchantCapabilities as the payment, under the same names. Otherwise it may show a card the payment then refuses. With usePaymentCheckout, pass them from paymentRequest. With an unknown network, auth method or merchant capability, the button keeps its previous configuration, or does not appear on the first render, and logs an error in debug builds. GooglePayButtonType: 'buy' | 'book' | 'checkout' | 'donate' | 'order' | 'pay' | 'subscribe' | 'plain'

import { GooglePayButton } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' import { callback } from 'react-native-nitro-modules' const handlePayment = async () => { // Call startPayment() from usePaymentCheckout here } <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" radius={8} supportedNetworks={['visa', 'mastercard']} onPress={callback(handlePayment)} style={{ width: '100%', height: 48 }} />
Same as Apple: onPress must be wrapped, as in onPress={callback(handlePayment)}. See Troubleshooting: Nitro callback for onPress.

usePaymentCheckout — Hook that provides cart and startPayment HybridPaymentHandler — Low-level API
Low-level API for payment operations. Use it when you need full control over the payment request and do not want the cart/state from usePaymentCheckout.
import { HybridPaymentHandler, createPaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay'

Resolves with whether the device supports the wallet and whether a card is ready. The check runs off the JS thread. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const status = await HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus({ supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION', }) // status: { isSupported: boolean, hasActiveCard: boolean } isSupported — The device can pay with Apple Pay / Google Pay, whether or not a card is set up. hasActiveCard — The user has a card ready on one of supportedNetworks. Pass the supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods and googlePayEnvironment your payment request uses (PayServiceStatusOptions); hasActiveCard then counts only cards the payment accepts. Without them, both platforms ask about visa, mastercard, amex and discover. The Promise rejects with the configuration error that would fail startPayment for a value the payment would refuse: an unknown network, capability or auth method, or no network the platform offers. A check that fails for any other reason resolves both flags as false. Without googlePayEnvironment, Android asks the TEST environment, where hasActiveCard is true whether or not the user has a card. What each platform checks, and which button to show, is in Check availability.

Starts the native payment flow with the given request. Returns a promise that resolves with the payment result. Pass the request through normalizePaymentRequest (or build it with createPaymentRequest) so amounts are validated before the sheet opens. See PaymentAmount. import { HybridPaymentHandler, normalizePaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment( normalizePaymentRequest({ merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex'], paymentItems: [{ label: 'Coffee Subscription', amount: '29.99', type: 'final' }], googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', }) ) // result: PaymentResult PaymentResult: interface PaymentResult extends PaymentDetails { status: 'success' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' code?: PaymentErrorCode // set when status isn't 'success' success: boolean // status === 'success' transactionId?: string // deprecated token?: PaymentToken error?: string // message for logs, also set on a cancel // From PaymentDetails, set only when requested: // billingContact, shippingContact, emailAddress, phoneNumber, shippingMethod } The promise resolves for every outcome, including a cancel and a misconfigured request; it doesn't reject. Branch on status and code. See Error codes for each code and PaymentResult for the fields. options.onAuthorize charges the token before the Apple Pay sheet closes. The result follows your callback: const result = await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request, { onAuthorize: async (token) => { const charged = await chargeOnServer(token) return charged ? { status: 'success' } : { status: 'failure', error: 'Payment failed' } }, }) See Charge before the sheet closes for the timeout and Android behavior. On iOS, the merchant ID is resolved from the app entitlements by default. Use applePayMerchantIdentifier only when you need to override the configured value at runtime. On iOS, the Apple Pay sheet lists your paymentItems and then a total labelled with merchantName ("Pay Your Store"). The library adds that total for you, so don't add your own "Total" item. Without merchantName, the total uses your app's display name. Build the request yourself or use createPaymentRequest for a single line item with defaults. Only one payment can be in flight at a time, on iOS and Android. A call made while another payment is still in progress, including one started by usePaymentCheckout, resolves immediately with { status: 'failed', code: 'IN_PROGRESS', success: false, error: 'A payment is already in progress' } and does not affect the payment in flight. A payment stays in flight until the native side settles it, right before its startPayment promise resolves. A new payment can start from that moment, even before your await continues. On iOS, the payment settles only after the Apple Pay sheet has closed. With onAuthorize, it also waits for your callback to settle or time out, so on iOS the payment ends once both have happened. Use isPaymentInProgress() to check first.

Synchronously returns whether a payment started with startPayment has not settled yet, including one started by usePaymentCheckout. While it returns true, startPayment resolves immediately with code: 'IN_PROGRESS'. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const isBusy = HybridPaymentHandler.isPaymentInProgress() startPayment still checks for itself, so you can call it without checking first. The check is useful when you keep your own state around a payment and don't want to update it for a call that never starts one. usePaymentCheckout uses it this way.

iOS only. Opens Wallet (Settings on iPad) so the user can add a card. Call it from a Set up Apple Pay button (ApplePayButton with buttonType="setUp") when isSupported is true and hasActiveCard is false. It does nothing on devices without Apple Pay, and nothing on Android, where the Google Pay sheet lets the user add a card. import { HybridPaymentHandler } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' HybridPaymentHandler.openPaymentSetup()

Custom checkout flow without the hook’s cart. One-off payments where you already have a full PaymentRequest. Flows that need full request control (for example shippingMethods, shippingType or a request built on your backend). Contact details such as shippingContactRequired work with both APIs; see Shipping and contact details. Need to check availability or supported networks without using usePaymentCheckout. For most apps, usePaymentCheckout is simpler: it builds the request from the cart and manages state.
createPaymentRequest — Build a request with defaults Types — PaymentRequest, PaymentResult, PaymentToken
TypeScript types exported from @gmisoftware/react-native-pay. Use them for request/result handling and server integration.

A monetary amount in the currency's major unit (dollars, not cents). type PaymentAmount = number | string Decimal string ('19.99'): exact. Must match ^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$; no exponents, spaces, or thousands separators. Number (19.99): read as the shortest decimal that round-trips, so 19.99 stays exactly 19.99. Results of float arithmetic such as 0.1 + 0.2 (0.30000000000000004) fail validation instead of being rounded. Before a payment starts, every amount is validated and sent to native code as a decimal string with the currency's number of decimal places (ISO 4217: 2 for USD, 0 for JPY, 3 for KWD). Native code converts it with NSDecimalNumber (iOS) and BigDecimal (Android), never through Double. A payment does not start when: an amount is not a finite number or a plain decimal string (NaN, Infinity, 'abc'); an amount has more decimal places than the currency allows (1.005 in USD, '1200.5' in JPY); the total of paymentItems is negative. Negative line items (discounts) are allowed. Google Pay accepts at most two decimal places, so on Android a three-decimal amount such as '1.234' KWD fails with an error.

A single line item (label, amount, type). interface PaymentItem { label: string amount: PaymentAmount // number | string type: 'final' | 'pending' } type is exported as PaymentItemType. final — Confirmed amount (e.g. product price, tax). pending — Estimate (e.g. shipping that may change). If any item is pending, the total is an estimate too: Google Pay receives totalPriceStatus: 'ESTIMATED' and Apple Pay marks the total summary item as .pending. Every item is sent to Google Pay as a LINE_ITEM display item, with status set to FINAL or PENDING.

Full request passed to the native layer (or to HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment). interface PaymentRequest { applePayMerchantIdentifier?: string merchantName?: string countryCode: string currencyCode: string paymentItems: PaymentItem[] merchantCapabilities: string[] supportedNetworks: string[] shippingType?: string // ShippingType value, iOS only shippingMethods?: ShippingMethod[] // → PaymentResult.shippingMethod billingContactRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.billingContact shippingContactRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.shippingContact emailRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.emailAddress phoneNumberRequired?: boolean // → PaymentResult.phoneNumber // Google Pay (Android) googlePayMerchantId?: string googlePayEnvironment?: 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' googlePayGateway?: string googlePayGatewayMerchantId?: string googlePayAllowedAuthMethods?: string[] // GooglePayAuthMethod values } On iOS, applePayMerchantIdentifier is optional and only needed when you want to override the Merchant ID configured in the native app entitlements. merchantName is the business name shown to the payer: the name on the Google Pay sheet and the label of the Apple Pay total. Apple Pay shows the last summary item as the total ("Pay label"), so on iOS the library appends a total item labelled with merchantName after your paymentItems, also when there is only one item. Don't add your own "Total" item. If merchantName is missing or blank, Android uses the app's label from the manifest and iOS uses the app's display name (CFBundleDisplayName, then CFBundleName). merchantCapabilities takes MerchantCapability values. supportedNetworks takes PaymentNetwork names, matched ignoring case, and limits the cards the payer can choose on both platforms. A name that is not a PaymentNetwork fails the payment with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and an error that contains Unknown payment network "<value>". Use a PaymentNetwork value such as "visa" or "mastercard". A network the platform does not offer is left out, so one cross-platform list works: Android drops cartesBancaires, for example. The payment fails when no network is left. googlePayAllowedAuthMethods takes GooglePayAuthMethod values and defaults to both. Android only. billingContactRequired, shippingContactRequired, emailRequired and phoneNumberRequired ask the payer for contact details, which come back in the result as PaymentDetails. On Android, a phone number is collected with an address. See Shipping and contact details. shippingType takes a ShippingType value. shippingMethods takes ShippingMethod values; the selected one is added to the total. The first is selected by default on iOS and is always the one charged on Android.

Returned from startPayment() (hook or handler). interface PaymentResult extends PaymentDetails { status: PaymentStatus // 'success' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' code?: PaymentErrorCode // set when status isn't 'success' success: boolean // status === 'success' transactionId?: string // deprecated token?: PaymentToken error?: string // message for logs, also set on a cancel // From PaymentDetails, set only when requested: // billingContact, shippingContact, emailAddress, phoneNumber, shippingMethod } type PaymentStatus = 'success' | 'cancelled' | 'failed' type PaymentErrorCode = | 'CANCELLED' | 'IN_PROGRESS' | 'CONFIGURATION' | 'NOT_AVAILABLE' | 'PROVIDER_ERROR' | 'UNKNOWN' status — 'cancelled' means the user closed the sheet before authorizing. It is not an error: usePaymentCheckout leaves error as null for it. code — Why the payment didn't succeed. 'CANCELLED' for a cancel, one of the others for a failure. See Error codes for what each one means and which native cases produce it. success — Kept for compatibility. Use status to tell a cancel from a failure. transactionId — Deprecated. A random ID the device generates for each successful result; it doesn't come from Apple, Google or your gateway. Don't use it as an idempotency key: use your order ID. token — Set on success. Send it to your backend to complete the charge with your gateway, unless onAuthorize already did. Contact details and shipping method — A successful result also holds the ones the request asked for; see PaymentDetails. error — A message for logs, such as 'Payment cancelled by user'. Don't match on it; use code.

Optional second argument of HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(). The hook takes onAuthorize in its config instead. interface StartPaymentOptions { onAuthorize?: ( token: PaymentToken, details: PaymentDetails ) => Promise<PaymentAuthorizationResult> } interface PaymentAuthorizationResult { status: 'success' | 'failure' error?: string // becomes PaymentResult.error, with code 'PROVIDER_ERROR', on failure } See Charge before the sheet closes.

The token you send to your server. Do not log or expose; treat as sensitive. interface PaymentToken { paymentMethod: PaymentMethod transactionIdentifier?: string paymentData: string // Opaque token payload (format depends on platform + gateway) } paymentMethod — Card/network and optional billing contact. transactionIdentifier — On iOS, Apple's identifier for the payment (PKPaymentToken.transactionIdentifier), generated on the device. Missing on Android: Google Pay doesn't return one. Key idempotency on your order ID instead. paymentData — Opaque payload for your gateway. iOS: Base64-encoded Apple Pay token data. Android: Google Pay tokenization payload (tokenizationData.token), gateway-dependent.

Describes the selected payment instrument. interface PaymentMethod { displayName?: string network?: PaymentNetwork type: PaymentMethodType secureElementPass?: PKSecureElementPass // iOS billingAddress?: CNContact // iOS } type PaymentMethodType = 'unknown' | 'debit' | 'credit' | 'prepaid' | 'store' PaymentMethodType is exported separately for direct typing. displayName — Describes the card to the payer, as the wallet words it: PKPaymentMethod.displayName on iOS, paymentMethodData.description on Android (for example "Visa •••• 1234"). Show it as is; don't parse it. network — The card's PaymentNetwork, or 'unknown' for a network the library cannot name. Use network rather than displayName for logic. type — How the card is funded: PKPaymentMethod.type on iOS, Google Pay's cardFundingSource on Android. Android reports 'credit', 'debit' or 'prepaid', and 'unknown' when Google Pay does not know; 'store' (a store card) is iOS only.

Card networks. Use these names in supportedNetworks; results report one of them in token.paymentMethod.network. type PaymentNetwork = | 'visa' | 'mastercard' | 'amex' | 'discover' | 'jcb' | 'maestro' | 'electron' | 'elo' | 'idcredit' | 'interac' | 'privateLabel' | 'cartesBancaires' | 'chinaUnionPay' | 'dankort' | 'eftpos' | 'girocard' | 'mada' | 'mir' | 'quicPay' | 'suica' | 'vPay' | 'waon' | 'nanaco' | 'bancontact' | 'postFinance' | 'pagoBancomat' | 'tmoney' | 'meeza' | 'napas' | 'bankAxept' | 'himyan' | 'jaywan' | 'myDebit' | 'unknown' // results only Platform Offers Google Pay visa, mastercard, amex, discover, jcb, interac, and electron, maestro and elo for Brazilian combo cards Apple Pay Every network but unknown. Some need a newer iOS: bancontact 16, postFinance 16.4, pagoBancomat and tmoney 17, meeza 17.4, napas and bankAxept 17.5, himyan and jaywan 18.4, myDebit 26 'unknown' is never a valid request value. A result reports it for a card on a network that is not listed here, instead of guessing.

Resolved by HybridPaymentHandler.payServiceStatus(). interface PayServiceStatus { isSupported: boolean // the device can pay with Apple Pay / Google Pay hasActiveCard: boolean // a card on the checked networks is ready } iOS Android isSupported PKPaymentAuthorizationViewController.canMakePayments() isReadyToPay hasActiveCard canMakePayments(usingNetworks:capabilities:) isReadyToPay with existingPaymentMethodRequired: true and the request's card parameters In the Google Pay TEST environment, hasActiveCard is true whether or not the user has a card. See Check availability.

What payServiceStatus checks. Pass the values your payment request uses, so hasActiveCard counts only cards the payment accepts. interface PayServiceStatusOptions { supportedNetworks?: string[] // default: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex', 'discover'] merchantCapabilities?: string[] // default: ['3DS'] googlePayAllowedAuthMethods?: string[] // Android only. Default: both googlePayEnvironment?: 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' // Android only. Default: 'TEST' } The values are checked as in startPayment, and the Promise rejects with the same configuration error for a value the payment would refuse.

Used in config and PaymentRequest for Android. type GooglePayEnvironment = 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' Use 'TEST' for development/sandbox; 'PRODUCTION' for live charges. Android uses 'TEST' when the value is omitted. See Testing payments.

How Google Pay may authenticate the card, used in googlePayAllowedAuthMethods (Android only). type GooglePayAuthMethod = 'PAN_ONLY' | 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' 'PAN_ONLY' — Cards saved to the payer's Google account. The token holds the card number. 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' — Cards tokenized on the device. The token holds a 3-D Secure cryptogram. Google Pay does not offer jcb or discover with it. The default is both. Pass ['CRYPTOGRAM_3DS'] when your gateway or Strong Customer Authentication requires device tokens. Android matches the values ignoring case, and any other value fails the payment with code: 'CONFIGURATION' and an error that contains Unknown Google Pay auth method "<value>". Use "PAN_ONLY" or "CRYPTOGRAM_3DS". They are separate from merchantCapabilities: every Apple Pay card is a device token, so iOS has nothing like 'PAN_ONLY'.

Merchant capabilities, used in merchantCapabilities. They come from Apple Pay; Android only reads 'Credit' and 'Debit'. type MerchantCapability = '3DS' | 'EMV' | 'Credit' | 'Debit' '3DS' and 'EMV' are Apple Pay payment protocols. PassKit needs at least one of them. EMV only covers China UnionPay, so every other card needs 3DS. Android ignores them. 'Credit' and 'Debit' limit the accepted card types. Both platforms match the values case-insensitively. Any other value fails the payment: the result has code: 'CONFIGURATION' and error: 'Unknown merchant capability "<value>". Use "3DS", "EMV", "Credit" or "Debit"'. iOS adds '3DS' when neither '3DS' nor 'EMV' is given, so [] is sent as 3DS and ['Credit'] as 3DS + Credit. Google Pay can leave credit cards out, but not debit cards: merchantCapabilities iOS accepts Android accepts ['3DS'] Every card type Every card type ['3DS', 'Debit'] Debit cards Every card type but credit cards ['3DS', 'Credit'] Credit cards Every card type ['3DS', 'Credit', 'Debit'] Credit and debit cards Every card type For 'Debit' without 'Credit', Android sends allowCreditCards: false to Google Pay, which UK gambling merchants must do. Prepaid cards stay allowed. To refuse debit cards on Android, check the card on your server before you charge it. Give GooglePayButton and payServiceStatus the same merchantCapabilities, so they are sent the same card types as the payment.

How Apple Pay labels the address, used in PaymentRequest.shippingType (iOS only; Android ignores the field). type ShippingType = 'shipping' | 'delivery' | 'storePickup' | 'servicePickup' For example, 'delivery' shows "Delivery Address" instead of "Shipping Address". Without shippingType, Apple Pay uses 'shipping'. Any other value fails the payment: the result has code: 'CONFIGURATION' and error: 'Unknown shipping type "<value>". Use "shipping", "delivery", "storePickup" or "servicePickup"'.

These iOS-only types appear in payment-related metadata returned by Apple Pay APIs (for example pass details tied to the selected card) and are mostly useful in advanced/native-integrated flows. type PassActivationState = | 'activated' | 'requiresActivation' | 'activating' | 'suspended' | 'deactivated' interface PKPass { passTypeIdentifier: string serialNumber: string organizationName?: string } interface PKSecureElementPass extends PKPass { primaryAccountIdentifier: string primaryAccountNumberSuffix: string deviceAccountIdentifier: string deviceAccountNumberSuffix: string passActivationState: PassActivationState devicePassIdentifier?: string pairedTerminalIdentifier?: string }

What the payer chose in the payment sheet besides the card, on both platforms. Each field is set only when the PaymentRequest asked for it. PaymentResult includes these fields, and onAuthorize receives them as its second argument. See Shipping and contact details. interface PaymentDetails { billingContact?: PaymentContact // billingContactRequired shippingContact?: PaymentContact // shippingContactRequired emailAddress?: string // emailRequired phoneNumber?: string // phoneNumberRequired, as the payer entered it shippingMethod?: ShippingMethod // the selected entry of shippingMethods }

A delivery option in PaymentRequest.shippingMethods. See Shipping methods. interface ShippingMethod { identifier: string // unique within the request, returned in PaymentResult.shippingMethod label: string // e.g. 'Express' amount: PaymentAmount // added to the total while selected; must not be negative detail?: string // e.g. 'Next business day' } The selected method appears as its own line in the sheet and is included in the total. PaymentResult.shippingMethod is the selected entry as you sent it. On Android, Google Pay cannot offer a choice yet, so the first method is charged and returned.

A name and postal address the payer chose. Parts the payer left empty are omitted. interface PaymentContact { name?: string // full name, e.g. 'Jane Appleseed' givenName?: string // iOS only familyName?: string // iOS only postalAddress?: CNPostalAddress } In postalAddress, street joins the address lines with '\n', isoCountryCode is uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2, and country (the country name) is iOS only.

CNPostalAddress is used by PaymentContact. The other types describe PaymentMethod.billingAddress, the card's billing contact on iOS. For a billing address on both platforms, use billingContactRequired and read PaymentResult.billingContact. type CNContactType = 'person' | 'organization' interface CNPhoneNumber { stringValue: string } interface CNPostalAddress { street?: string city?: string state?: string postalCode?: string country?: string isoCountryCode?: string } interface CNLabeledPhoneNumber { label?: string value: CNPhoneNumber } interface CNLabeledEmailAddress { label?: string value: string } interface CNLabeledPostalAddress { label?: string value: CNPostalAddress } interface CNContact { identifier: string contactType: CNContactType namePrefix: string givenName: string middleName: string familyName: string previousFamilyName: string nameSuffix: string nickname: string organizationName: string departmentName: string jobTitle: string phoneticGivenName: string phoneticMiddleName: string phoneticFamilyName: string phoneticOrganizationName?: string note: string imageDataAvailable?: boolean phoneNumbers: CNLabeledPhoneNumber[] emailAddresses: CNLabeledEmailAddress[] postalAddresses: CNLabeledPostalAddress[] }
type ApplePayStatus = PayServiceStatus
The main hook for payment checkout. It handles availability, cart state, and payment processing so you can focus on UI and sending the token to your server.
import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay'

Pass a single config object. iOS reads the Apple Pay merchant ID from the native app configuration. Use applePayMerchantIdentifier only if you need to override it at runtime. Source of truth for these types: package/src/hooks/usePaymentCheckout.ts. interface UsePaymentCheckoutConfig { merchantName?: string // business name shown on the sheet countryCode?: string // default: 'US' currencyCode?: string // default: 'USD' supportedNetworks?: string[] // default: ['visa', 'mastercard', 'amex', 'discover'] merchantCapabilities?: MerchantCapability[] // default: ['3DS'] applePayMerchantIdentifier?: string // optional iOS override // Google Pay (Android) googlePayMerchantId?: string googlePayEnvironment?: 'TEST' | 'PRODUCTION' googlePayGateway?: string googlePayGatewayMerchantId?: string googlePayAllowedAuthMethods?: GooglePayAuthMethod[] // default: both // Contact details, returned in the result billingContactRequired?: boolean shippingContactRequired?: boolean emailRequired?: boolean phoneNumberRequired?: boolean // Charge the token before the sheet closes onAuthorize?: ( token: PaymentToken, details: PaymentDetails ) => Promise<PaymentAuthorizationResult> } merchantName — The business name shown to the payer. On iOS, Apple Pay labels the total with it, so the sheet reads "Pay merchantName". On Android, it is the merchant name on the Google Pay sheet. Without it, iOS uses your app's display name (CFBundleDisplayName) and Android uses the app's label. Set it on both platforms. supportedNetworks — The card networks the payer can choose, as PaymentNetwork names. Both platforms honour it. A network the platform does not offer is left out, and an unknown name fails the payment. Pass the same list to GooglePayButton. googlePayAllowedAuthMethods — Android only. Which Google Pay cards to accept: 'PAN_ONLY' (saved to the Google account), 'CRYPTOGRAM_3DS' (tokenized on the device), or both, the default. See GooglePayAuthMethod. merchantCapabilities — The card types to accept and, on iOS, the payment protocols. iOS adds '3DS' when neither '3DS' nor 'EMV' is given. On Android only 'Debit' without 'Credit' has an effect: it leaves credit cards out. Google Pay cannot leave debit cards out, so ['3DS', 'Credit'] accepts every card type on Android. An unknown value fails the payment on both platforms. Pass the same list to GooglePayButton. See MerchantCapability. supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods, googlePayEnvironment — Also used for the availability check, which fails like the payment for a value the payment would refuse. Set googlePayEnvironment: 'PRODUCTION' in a live app: in TEST, Google Pay reports a card whether or not there is one. billingContactRequired, shippingContactRequired, emailRequired, phoneNumberRequired — Ask the payer for a billing address, a shipping address, an email address or a phone number. They come back as result.billingContact, result.shippingContact, result.emailAddress and result.phoneNumber. See Shipping and contact details. onAuthorize — Called with the token and the requested contact details after the user authorizes the payment. Charge it on your server and resolve with { status: 'success' } or { status: 'failure', error }. See Charge before the sheet closes. An inline function is fine: startPayment() uses the one from the latest render, and a payment keeps that function until it settles, even if the config changes meanwhile.

interface UsePaymentCheckoutReturn { // Availability isSupported: boolean hasActiveCard: boolean isCheckingStatus: boolean refreshStatus: () => void // Cart items: PaymentItem[] total: number addItem: (label: string, amount: PaymentAmount, type?: 'final' | 'pending') => void addItems: (items: Array<{ label: string; amount: PaymentAmount; type?: 'final' | 'pending' }>) => void removeItem: (index: number) => void updateItem: (index: number, updates: Partial<PaymentItem>) => void clearItems: () => void // Payment startPayment: () => Promise<PaymentResult | null> isProcessing: boolean result: PaymentResult | null // last result; check result.status error: Error | null // null after a cancel // Utilities reset: () => void paymentRequest: PaymentRequest } isSupported — The device can pay with Apple Pay / Google Pay, whether or not a card is set up. hasActiveCard — The user has a card ready on one of supportedNetworks. See PayServiceStatus for what each platform checks. isCheckingStatus — true until the availability check settles. The hook checks on mount and again when supportedNetworks, merchantCapabilities, googlePayAllowedAuthMethods or googlePayEnvironment change. The check never blocks the JS thread. refreshStatus() — Checks availability again, for example when the app returns from Wallet after openPaymentSetup(). isCheckingStatus is true until it settles, and the flags keep their last values meanwhile. Which button to show for each combination is in Check availability. items / total — Current cart and its exact decimal total, as a number (NaN if an amount is invalid). Amounts are number | string (PaymentAmount); use formatAmount(item.amount, currencyCode) to display them. startPayment() — Opens the native sheet. Returns Promise<PaymentResult | null>. Returns null and sets error when the cart is empty. Returns null and sets error, without opening the sheet, when an amount is invalid or the total is negative (see PaymentAmount). Returns the native PaymentResult when the sheet closes. Check status and code (see Error codes). A cancel returns status: 'cancelled' and code: 'CANCELLED'. It sets result but leaves error as null, so the user closing the sheet doesn't show up as a failed payment. Any other failure from the native flow returns status: 'failed' with its code, and sets error to an Error with the result's message. Returns null if an exception is thrown while starting/processing the payment. With onAuthorize, resolves after your callback settles. A 'failure' result becomes { status: 'failed', code: 'PROVIDER_ERROR', error } and sets error. Returns { status: 'failed', code: 'IN_PROGRESS', success: false, error: 'A payment is already in progress' } without opening a second sheet if a payment is still in flight, whether this hook, another usePaymentCheckout or HybridPaymentHandler started it. isProcessing, result and error stay as they were. This check comes first, so it also applies when the cart is empty. paymentRequest / startPayment — Keep their identity until a config value or the cart changes. The hook compares the config by value (arrays such as supportedNetworks by content), so an inline config object is fine, and both are safe as hook dependencies and props of memoized components. reset() — Clears result and error (does not clear cart). It does not clear isProcessing while a payment is in flight; isProcessing becomes false when that payment settles.

import { usePaymentCheckout } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const { isSupported, items, total, addItem, addItems, removeItem, startPayment, isProcessing, error, reset, } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', currencyCode: 'USD', countryCode: 'US', googlePayMerchantId: 'your_google_pay_merchant_id', googlePayEnvironment: 'TEST', googlePayGateway: 'stripe', googlePayGatewayMerchantId: 'your_stripe_merchant_id', }) // Single item addItem('Product', 29.99) // Multiple items; amounts can be numbers or decimal strings addItems([ { label: 'Product', amount: 29.99 }, { label: 'Shipping', amount: '5.00' }, { label: 'Tax', amount: 2.8, type: 'final' }, ]) const result = await startPayment() if (result?.status === 'success' && result.token) { // Send result.token to your server } // 'cancelled': the user closed the sheet; `error` stays null. // 'failed': `error` is set, and result.code says why.
If you call startPayment() when items.length === 0, the hook sets error to a “Cart is empty” error and returns null. Add at least one item before starting payment.

Use usePaymentCheckout when you want cart state + defaults managed in React state. Use HybridPaymentHandler when you need to build the full PaymentRequest yourself (for example shippingMethods, shippingType or prebuilt request payloads from your backend). The hook's total covers only the cart, so it doesn't take shippingMethods. Utility helpers for this path are documented in Utility functions.
Components (ApplePayButton / GooglePayButton) HybridPaymentHandler — Low-level API Types — PaymentItem, PaymentResult, PaymentRequest, etc.
Helpers for building payment requests, items, and formatting. All are exported from @gmisoftware/react-native-pay.

Use these functions when you are building a manual or low-level flow (usually with HybridPaymentHandler) and need to assemble PaymentRequest data yourself. If you use usePaymentCheckout, cart state and request building are handled for you internally, so these helpers are optional.

Builds a full PaymentRequest with one line item and sensible defaults. Required: amount, label. Defaults: countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', supportedNetworks: [CommonNetworks], merchantCapabilities: ['3DS']. The amount is validated with normalizePaymentRequest, so createPaymentRequest throws for an invalid amount, and the returned request holds it as a decimal string. import { createPaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const request = createPaymentRequest({ amount: 29.99, // or '29.99' label: 'Coffee Subscription', merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', // Optional: applePayMerchantIdentifier, googlePayMerchantId, // googlePayEnvironment, googlePayGateway, googlePayGatewayMerchantId, etc. }) // request.paymentItems is a single item: [{ label: 'Coffee Subscription', amount: '29.99', type: 'final' }] Use with HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request) for a manual flow.

Validates every amount in paymentItems and shippingMethods and returns a copy in which each amount is a decimal string with the currency's number of decimal places. See PaymentAmount for the rules. Call it before passing a request you built yourself to HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment. createPaymentRequest and usePaymentCheckout already call it. import { HybridPaymentHandler, normalizePaymentRequest } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const request = normalizePaymentRequest({ countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', paymentItems: [ { label: 'Book', amount: 19.9, type: 'final' }, { label: 'Discount', amount: '-5', type: 'final' }, ], supportedNetworks: ['visa', 'mastercard'], merchantCapabilities: ['3DS'], }) // request.paymentItems amounts: '19.90', '-5.00' await HybridPaymentHandler.startPayment(request) normalizePaymentRequest({ ...request, paymentItems: [{ label: 'Fee', amount: 1.005, type: 'final' }] }) // throws: Amount for "Fee" has more than 2 decimal places, which USD allows, got 1.005

Creates a single PaymentItem. import { createPaymentItem } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' createPaymentItem('Subscription', 29.99, 'final') createPaymentItem('Shipping', '5.00', 'pending') // type defaults to 'final' The amount is stored as given and validated when the payment starts.

Sums the amount of all items with exact decimal arithmetic, the same as native code, and returns the sum as a number. Returns NaN if an amount is invalid. import { calculateTotal, createPaymentItem } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' const items = [ createPaymentItem('Product', 29.99), createPaymentItem('Tax', '2.40'), ] calculateTotal(items) // 32.39 calculateTotal([createPaymentItem('A', 0.1), createPaymentItem('B', 0.2)]) // 0.3, not 0.30000000000000004

Formats a number or decimal string with the currency's number of decimal places (two when currencyCode is omitted), rounding half away from zero. Returns 'NaN' for an invalid amount. import { formatAmount } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' formatAmount(29.9) // "29.90" formatAmount('100') // "100.00" formatAmount(1.005) // "1.01" formatAmount(1500, 'JPY') // "1500"
Parses a string to a number. import { parseAmount } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' parseAmount('29.99') // 29.99 parseAmount('100') // 100

Returns whether network is in supportedNetworks (case-insensitive). import { isNetworkSupported } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' isNetworkSupported('visa', ['visa', 'mastercard']) // true isNetworkSupported('AMEX', ['visa', 'amex']) // true isNetworkSupported('discover', ['visa', 'mastercard']) // false

Returns a human-readable name for a payment network. import { formatNetworkName } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' formatNetworkName('visa') // "Visa" formatNetworkName('amex') // "American Express" formatNetworkName('mastercard') // "Mastercard" formatNetworkName('unknown') // "Unknown"

Constants for common network IDs (for building supportedNetworks): import { CommonNetworks } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' CommonNetworks.VISA // 'visa' CommonNetworks.MASTERCARD // 'mastercard' CommonNetworks.AMEX // 'amex' CommonNetworks.DISCOVER // 'discover' Use with createPaymentRequest or when building a PaymentRequest by hand.
Supported versions and upgrade notes.

react — * (compatible with current React 18/19) react-native — * (0.70+ recommended) react-native-nitro-modules — >= 0.36.0 (required) expo — >= 53.0.0 (if using Expo; tested with SDK 57 / React Native 0.86) Android minSdkVersion — 26+ (required for Nitro Modules prefab) Install the correct Nitro version first; the payment library depends on it.
React Native 0.70 or newer (0.86 with Expo SDK 57) Expo 53–57 when using Expo

merchantIdentifier — Optional in the plugin config. If omitted, Apple Pay entitlements are not added (use for Android-only or when you add Apple Pay later). enableGooglePay — Defaults to false. Set to true to enable Google Pay on Android.

Platform Apple Pay Google Pay iOS Yes (ApplePayButton, usePaymentCheckout, HybridPaymentHandler) N/A (use Google Pay on Android) Android N/A Yes (GooglePayButton, usePaymentCheckout, HybridPaymentHandler) Use Platform.OS (or equivalent) to render the correct button and to pass platform-specific config (e.g. Google Pay options only on Android).

Regenerated Nitrogen bindings for react-native-nitro-modules 0.36+ (Expo SDK 57 / React Native 0.86). Peer dependency react-native-nitro-modules is now >= 0.36.0 (was >= 0.35.0). Example app upgraded to Expo SDK 57 (React Native 0.86, React 19.2.3).

Regenerated Nitrogen bindings for react-native-nitro-modules 0.35+ (JavaPart/CxxPart JNI model). Peer dependency react-native-nitro-modules is now >= 0.35.0 (was >= 0.31.4). Android minSdkVersion 26+ is required (Nitro Modules prefab). Set minSdkVersion to at least 26 in expo-build-properties or your app's build.gradle. Consumers on nitro 0.31.x must stay on 0.0.14 or upgrade nitro-modules first. Check the package changelog or GitHub releases for version-specific notes. When upgrading, run npx expo prebuild --clean and re-test on both platforms. If you use TypeScript, run bun run typecheck (or your typecheck script) after upgrading.

Do I need Expo? No. The library works in bare React Native too. The Expo plugin only simplifies adding Apple Pay entitlements and Google Pay metadata; in a bare project you configure those in Xcode and Android Studio yourself. Can I use only Apple Pay or only Google Pay? Yes. Omit enableGooglePay (or set false) for iOS-only; omit plugin merchantIdentifier for Android-only. In code, only render the button for the platform you support. Which gateways are supported for Google Pay? Any gateway that supports the Google Pay API and the gateway token format. Commonly used: Stripe, Braintree, Square, Adyen, Authorize.net, Checkout.com. Set googlePayMerchantId, googlePayGateway, and googlePayGatewayMerchantId accordingly. Where do I report issues? GitHub Issues.
The repository includes a full example app in the example/ folder: an Expo app that demonstrates the checkout flow with usePaymentCheckout, cart management, and platform-specific buttons.

From example/app/(tabs)/index.tsx: import { Platform } from 'react-native' import { ApplePayButton, GooglePayButton, usePaymentCheckout, } from '@gmisoftware/react-native-pay' import { callback } from 'react-native-nitro-modules' const { isSupported, isCheckingStatus, items, total, addItems, clearItems, startPayment, isProcessing, reset, } = usePaymentCheckout({ merchantName: 'Your Store', countryCode: 'US', currencyCode: 'USD', }) const handleAddCoffee = () => { clearItems() addItems([ { label: 'Coffee', amount: 4.99 }, { label: 'Tax', amount: 0.5 }, ]) } const handlePayment = async () => { const paymentResult = await startPayment() if (paymentResult?.status === 'success') { reset() clearItems() } } {Platform.OS === 'ios' ? ( <ApplePayButton buttonType="buy" buttonStyle="black" onPress={callback(handlePayment)} style={{ width: '100%', height: 56 }} /> ) : ( <GooglePayButton buttonType="buy" theme="dark" radius={8} onPress={callback(handlePayment)} style={{ width: '100%', height: 56 }} /> )}

Checkout flow — Add items (e.g. “Coffee”, “Subscription”), see cart and total, then pay with Apple Pay or Google Pay. Status — Check whether the device can make payments or only set up cards. Cart UI — Add/clear items and display total. Result handling — Success and error messages; reset and clear cart after success. Nitro callback — Buttons use callback(handlePayment) (see Troubleshooting: Nitro callback for onPress).
From the repo root: cd example bun install npx expo prebuild npx expo run:ios # or npx expo run:android Or from the root (if scripts are set up): bun run ios # or bun run android

Use the checkout screen in the example app as a reference for: Calls usePaymentCheckout with countryCode, currencyCode, and optional platform-specific overrides. Shows a loading state while isCheckingStatus is true. Renders “Quick Add” buttons that call addItems or addItem. Displays the cart (items + total) and a “Clear” action. Renders ApplePayButton on iOS and GooglePayButton on Android with callback(handlePayment). On successful payment, shows an alert and calls reset() and clearItems(). Copy these patterns into your app: config setup, cart handling, button usage, and native-safe onPress handlers.
